thread:
PagerBot: :rotating_light: HIGH - GPU pool 'east-prod-gpu' exceeding throttle threshold (queue growth). Current queued reqs: 1830, serving capacity: 42 GPUs. autoscaler_max=45, autoscaler_desired=42. prefix_cache_miss_rate jumped to 67%.
Ken (oncall): seeing alerts, joining. Paging SREs.
Priya G.: on it, checking console graphs now. Thoughts: autoscaler might be hitting max or stuck, or continuous-batching param causing longer in-flight windows.
Miguel R.: I see the same. autoscaler API shows "scale_up_in_progress" for 12m but failed to handshake with cloud provider. Error: `RateLimitExceeded` on scaling calls.
Sophie L. (SRE): confirmed. Also seeing KV prefix cache eviction spikes right before queue ramp. prefix_cache_miss_rate timeline: 5m avg 12% -> spike 67% at 3437212120. That explains throughput drop.
Ken (oncall): customer impact? any 5xxs?
Priya G.: Some 429 throttles and token timeouts for tail latencies >10s. We have a few support tickets citing slow generation. Not full outage but severe degradation for heavier prompts.
Miguel R.: Quick mitigation proposal: 1) pause continuous batching (set `continuous_batching.enabled=false`) on production route groups; 2) reduce default batch_size from 512 -> 256 to unblock long tail; 3) temporarily increase autoscaler max to 60 while we validate cloud API.
Sophie L. (SRE): +1. Also we should route high-priority customers to fallback pool `east-prod-gpu-fallback` which still has free capacity. Add route weight 10% -> fallback.
Ken (oncall): do the mitigations one at a time. Priya, can you flip continuous batching? Miguel, can you run the scale up? Sophie, monitor cache miss and queue. I'll coordinate comms.
Priya G.: flipping continuous batching off now. Command: ```infractl route update --env prod --setting continuous_batching=false```
InfraBot: Command accepted. Rolling change to 64 route workers.
Priya G.: done. Observing immediate decrease in average in-flight window. queue growth rate slowed but not yet reversing.
Miguel R.: hitting cloud provider rate limit when calling scale API. Retrying with exponential backoff and batching requests. Running: ```cloudctl autoscale update --pool east-prod-gpu --max 60 --retry 5```
InfraBot: autoscaler update acknowledged, queued.
Sophie L. (SRE): starting cache investigation: fetching prefix cache stats. snippet:
```
prefix_cache: hit_rate=0.33, miss_rate=0.67, eviction_rate=0.18, shard_hot=kv-12
kvstore: pending_evictions=12, avg_ttl_ms=45000
```
Sophie L. (SRE): looks like a recent rollout to `kvstore` (shard rotation) reduced hot-cache residency. I'm rolling a mitigation: increase prefix_cache_ttl for hot keys and pin top 50 prefixes.
Miguel R.: autoscaler update eventually succeeded. Desired nodes -> 58. New GPUs coming up, ETA ~3m.
Ken (oncall): good. Sophie, any change after TTL bump?
Sophie L. (SRE): 2m after TTL bump: miss_rate -> 45%, eviction_rate down to 0.06. queue dropping slightly. Latency p95 from 9.8s -> 6.2s.
Priya G.: re-enabled route-level priority for enterprise customers to route to fallback pool. Command: ```routectl weight set --route /v1/generate --pool east-prod-fallback --weight 0.15```
PagerBot: Notifying on-call rotation and triggering incident channel update.
Ken (oncall): I'm posting a quick customer advisory: "We are experiencing degraded latency due to increased inference queueing in east region. Working on autoscaler/backfill. Some requests may see higher latencies or 429s. ETA improvement ~10-20m."
Miguel R.: new nodes are up. Throughput per GPU still low compared to baseline - suspect batching config isn't matching new node behavior. Investigating continuous-batching params (window_ms, max_inflight_bytes).
Sophie L. (SRE): found that a recent config rollout (config v2026.11.3) changed `continuous_batching.window_ms` from 18 -> 120 for some routes (accidental). That expands batch windows and increases tail latencies for heterogeneous prompt sizes, causing queue build. Reverting that file now.
Priya G.: revert command: ```configctl rollback --service routing --version v2026.11.3```
InfraBot: rollback in progress.
Sophie L. (SRE): after revert, window_ms back to 18. Observing batch size distribution normalize (fewer huge batches). p95 latency trending down. queue length 1830 -> 820 over 12m.
Ken (oncall): great. Any lingering customer facing errors?
Priya G.: a small percentage still see 429s for heavy streaming flows. We'll keep fallback routing for the next 30m. Open incidents: two P1 support tickets for premium customers; escalated to SE team.
Miguel R.: recording actions for postmortem: autoscaler rate limit handling needs backoff + queuing, config rollout validation must include continuous-batching param guardrails, topology-aware prefix cache pinning to reduce miss storms.
Sophie L. (SRE): also add healthcheck for prefix_cache_miss_rate > 30% -> alert before queues hit 1000.
Ken (oncall): handing off to night oncall (Sophie) in 18m. I'll summarize state and runbook: mitigations applied - continuous batching disabled, routing fallback enabled, autoscaler increased, prefix cache TTL bump and config rollback. Current status: queue building reversed, miss rate down to 28%, p95 latency 3.1s, no new 5xxs but some 429s.
Ken (oncall): passing to Sophie L. (SRE) for monitoring and postmortem. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
Sophie L. (SRE): taking it. I'll keep the channel updated every 15m and draft the incident timeline.
PagerBot: Incident annotated: severity=SEV2, start_ts=3437212345, mitigation_ts=3437212550, recover_ts=3437213620.
Ken (oncall): closing active pager. If anything spikes, re-open channel.
Sophie L. (SRE): quick note for postmortem: impact window ~ 40 minutes, customers affected: 12 accounts with elevated latency, 2 rate-limited. Root causes: autoscaler rate-limits + bad config rollout (continuous_batching.window_ms) + KV prefix cache eviction storm. Remediation: autopolicy for autoscaler retry/backoff, config gating for batching params, deploy pinned prefix caching for hot prefixes.
Priya G.: filing incident ticket and alert rules update after this.
Sophie L. (SRE): handoff complete. Monitoring only.
